findings.title: Radar Instrument Readability
findings.where: Arena and Road screens, bottom-left corner
findings.problem: The radar is a dark disc with a very faint green sweep and no distinct grid or contact blips. It looks like a dead pixel or a broken texture rather than a functional instrument.
findings.why: In a vehicular combat game, situational awareness is critical. If the radar looks broken or is too dark to read at a glance, players will ignore it, leading to unfair hits and frustration.
findings.fix: Increase the brightness and contrast of the sweep line (e.g., bright cyan or green), add a visible grid (crosshairs), and ensure enemy contacts appear as high-contrast bright dots.

findings.title: Constructor Preview Mismatch
findings.where: Constructor screen, right panel under 'SUBCOMPACT - TOP VIEW'
findings.problem: The car visualization is a generic blue rounded rectangle with abstract inner boxes. It bears no resemblance to the detailed orange vehicle sprite seen in the Arena, Road, and City screens.
findings.why: This creates a cognitive disconnect. Players cannot visualize their build choices in the constructor, making the customization phase feel abstract and detached from the actual gameplay.
findings.fix: Replace the abstract blue schematic with the actual top-down sprite of the player's car (the orange one), or a detailed wireframe that matches the game's art style.

findings.title: City Interaction Markers
findings.where: City screen, small yellow chevrons next to buildings
findings.problem: The interaction points (building entrances) are marked by tiny yellow arrows that blend into the grey, cracked ground texture. They lack visual weight.
findings.why: The tutorial text instructs players to 'head into a building', but the visual cues are too subtle. Players may drive past objectives or feel lost because the interactable elements don't pop.
findings.fix: Scale up the markers by 2x, add a subtle glow or pulsing animation, and use a color that contrasts sharply with the grey ground (like the UI cyan or the car's orange).

findings.title: Weapon List Visual Density
findings.problem: The weapon slots are displayed as a long, dense list of text rows all reading '(empty)'. It resembles a raw database dump or spreadsheet rather than a game interface.
findings.why: It looks unfinished and overwhelming. It wastes vertical space and doesn't invite interaction. Players won't intuitively know they can click or select these rows to add gear.
findings.fix: Convert the list into a grid of icon slots (e.g., 2 columns of 5). Empty slots should show a faint 'plus' icon or a dashed border to indicate they are drop zones or selectable.

findings.title: Title Menu Styling
findings.problem: The menu box is a simple rectangle with a thin cyan border and plain text. It looks like a default HTML form or a debug overlay, clashing with the high-quality, atmospheric tank artwork behind it.
findings.why: The title screen sets the first impression. A raw, unstyled menu box makes the game look like a prototype or a jam game, undermining the production value of the background art.
findings.fix: Give the menu box a solid, semi-transparent dark background (matching the UI panels), use a distinct highlight bar for the selected item (instead of just a border), and ensure the font matches the terminal aesthetic of the rest of the UI.
